newsitem.title: FRANCE: French Greens want Superphenix plant closed.
newsitem.headline: French Greens want Superphenix plant closed.

text.p: France's Greens urged the centre-right government on Monday to close the prototype Superphenix fast-breeder nuclear reactor, which they dubbed "a technological, economic and political mistake".
The Council of State last week cancelled a decree dating from July 1994 which authorised the restart of the 1,200 megawatt plant, which has been on hold since December.

Following an appeal from environmentalists, the Council ruled that the procedure for the plant's transformation into a research and demonstration prototype was irregular and required a new public inquiry.
The government can now either modify the decree or launch a new inquiry, which would take more time and be politically more risky, an Industry Ministry official said.
In an open letter to Prime Minister Alain Juppe, Greens leader Dominique Voynet urged him to take advantage of the Council ruling to put a stop to financial waste.
The Greens "will take all legal measures necessary" to ensure the plant, which is located near the southeastern Alpine city of Grenoble, is not reopened, she wrote.
The 60 billion franc ($10.5 billion) Superphenix reactor has had a troubled history. Since it was commissioned 20 years ago it has operated for only a dozen months.
